blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Self-supervised vision transformers are increasingly used as reusable encoders for Earth observation, but their inference cost on the hardware available in the field is rarely characterized. We deploy a pretrained SAR-optical masked-autoencoder encoder on three commodity x86 nodes, from a low-power CPU without AVX2 to an AVX2+VNNI reference, at FP32, FP16 and INT8 on the CPU and, where present, the integrated GPU, and report latency, energy (RAPL and wall plug) and linear-probe accuracy. Quantization is accuracy-neutral: INT8 changes micro-mAP by only +0.0006, within the seed spread, so precision becomes a pure cost decision. INT8 lowers CPU latency on every node, by 1.45x even on the CPU without AVX2, and CPU energy wherever it is measured, and the VNNI reference (1.53x) suggests a further gain beyond AVX2. The Pareto-optimal device shifts from the integrated GPU, which is 4.38x faster than the CPU on the weakest node, to the CPU as the CPU class improves.
blocks.zh: 自我监督的视觉变压器被越来越多地用作地球观测的可重复使用的编码器,但是它们对于实地可用的硬件的推论成本却很少被定性. 我们在3个商品x86节点上安装了经过预先训练的SAR-光学掩码-自动编码器,从没有AVX2的低功率CPU到AVX2+VNNI参考,在CPU上安装了FP32,FP16和INT8,在目前情况下安装了综合GPU,并报告纬度,能(RAPL和墙插)和线性探测精度. 量子化是精度中性的:INT8在种子传播范围内仅将微米马普改变为+0.06,因此精度成为纯粹的成本决定. INT8将每个节点上CPU的活性降低1.45x,甚至在没有AVX2的CPU上也降低1.45x,无论在哪里测量CPU能量,而VNNI参考值(1.53x)则暗示了AVX2之外的进一步增益. 帕雷托-优化设备从集成GPU(比最弱节点上的CPU快4.38x)转向CPU,随着CPU类的改进.

blocks.en: I Introduction
blocks.zh: 一. 导言

blocks.en:
Self-supervised pretraining is now a standard way to build reusable encoders for
Earth observation, where unlabeled Sentinel imagery is abundant but labels are
scarce. Masked autoencoders [ 1 ] over the vision
transformer [ 2 ] are a common choice, evaluated on archives
such as BigEarthNet [ 3 ] and its refined release
reBEN [ 4 ] ; the encoder studied here [ 5 ] follows this recipe on a joint SAR–optical corpus.

自我监督的预训现在是建立可重复使用的编码器的标准方式。
地球观测,无标签的哨兵图像丰富但标签是
紧缺。 蒙面自动编码器在视野上
变压器[2]是一个常见的选择,在档案中进行评估
例如大地球网[3]及其精细的发布
reBEN [4];此处研究的编码器遵循了这个关于SAR-光学联合体的配方。

blocks.en:
Most of this work is evaluated on accuracy alone, yet an encoder is only useful
if one inference is cheap enough for the hardware actually available, often a
small, passively cooled x86 box rather than a server GPU. The cost of that inference,
and how it responds to post-training quantization, depends on details that are
seldom reported: whether the CPU offers wide SIMD (AVX2) or integer
dot-product instructions (VNNI), and whether a usable integrated GPU (iGPU) is
present. These features vary widely across commodity hardware, so a single
benchmark number does not tell a practitioner what to deploy.

如果一个推论对实际可用的硬件来说是便宜的, 经常是一个

现在。 这些特性在商品硬件上差异很大,所以只有一个
基准数不会告诉从业者要部署什么。

blocks.en:
Running learned models close to the sensor is already an active topic in Earth
observation, but most of the work targets dedicated accelerators on board. Φ \Phi -Sat-1 flew a convolutional cloud detector on an Intel Myriad 2 vision
processing unit [ 6 ] , RaVÆn sizes a variational
autoencoder for change detection on resource-limited flight
hardware [ 7 ] , and Ziaja et al. benchmark deep models for
on-board use [ 8 ] . On the model side, post-training
quantization of vision transformers is known to be delicate, since post-softmax,
post-GELU and LayerNorm activations are hard to quantize, and dedicated schemes
have been proposed for it [ 9 , 10 ] . Much less is known
about the general-purpose x86 hardware available on the ground, in small,
passively cooled boxes, some of which still lack AVX2, and about how a
self-supervised SAR–optical transformer behaves there when latency, energy and
accuracy are measured together.

blocks.en:
This letter characterizes the deployment of this encoder across a gradient of
commodity x86 classes. Our contributions are: (i) we show that quantization is accuracy-neutral for this
SAR–optical encoder, so precision becomes a pure cost decision; (ii) we
characterize that cost across an ISA-capability gradient and show that INT8 pays
off even on a CPU without AVX2, with a present-day VNNI reference indicating a
further gain beyond AVX2; and (iii) using a reproducible RAPL plus
wall-plug protocol, we show that the Pareto-optimal device is not fixed but moves
from the iGPU to the CPU as the CPU class improves.

blocks.en: II Materials and Methods
blocks.zh: 二. 材料和方法

blocks.en: II-A Encoder, Intermediate Representation and Task
blocks.zh: II-A 编码员、中级代表和任务

blocks.en:
We study the encoder released with [ 5 ] , a ViT-S/16
masked autoencoder [ 1 , 2 ] pretrained in a
self-supervised manner on the STRATA-S12 SAR–optical corpus and archived with
it [ 11 ] . The input stacks
six co-registered optical and SAR channels and the model returns a 384-D class
token; we deploy only the encoder, with no decoder and no masking. The encoder is
rebuilt from timm [ 12 ] transformer blocks, exported to ONNX and compiled to
OpenVINO [ 13 ] intermediate
representations (IR) at FP32, FP16 and INT8. INT8 uses post-training
quantization [ 14 ] with
NNCF [ 15 ] on a real calibration subset of
512 reBEN patches, disjoint from train and test. The IRs are built
once with the development toolchain and shipped unchanged, so a given precision
yields identical outputs on every host: accuracy is a property of the IR and is
measured once.
Representation quality is assessed on reBEN [ 4 ] as a
19-class multi-label task through a linear probe on frozen
features (20000 training and 10000 test patches, three
seeds), following the protocol of [ 5 ] as implemented in
its public evaluation harness [ 16 ] ; we report micro- and
macro-mAP and the change in micro-mAP relative to FP32.

blocks.en: II-B Hardware Gradient
blocks.zh: II-B 硬件梯度

blocks.en:
We deploy on three commodity x86 nodes chosen to span a gradient of SIMD
capability rather than of price (Table I ): a floor node without
AVX2, a mainstream AVX2 step node, and an AVX2+VNNI reference node,
names used throughout the letter. The first two also carry an
Intel integrated GPU (iGPU) and act as edge targets; the reference is used for
CPU latency only, as a present-day point of comparison rather than as an edge
target. The OpenVINO runtime is pinned to a single release on all three nodes so
that the CPU and iGPU paths stay comparable.

blocks.zh: 二-C 计量议定书

For each node, device and precision the IR is compiled and run for W = 20 W=20 discarded warm-up passes, followed by R = 5 R=5 repetitions of N = 200 N=200 forward passes at batch size one (single
stream). Latency is the wall-clock time of a repetition divided by N N , reported
as the mean with a 95% confidence interval (Student’s t t ) over the repetitions.

blocks.en: III-B INT8 Lowers Cost on the CPU; FP16 Does Not
blocks.zh: CPU成本降低; FP16 不降低

blocks.en:
On the CPU, FP16 brings no benefit: it is essentially tied with FP32, and on the
step node it is even slightly slower (35.74 vs
33.80 ms). INT8, in contrast, is faster on every node:
1.45 × \times over FP32 on the floor node,
1.27 × \times on the step node and
1.53 × \times on the reference (Fig. 1 ).
Energy tracks latency both at the CPU package and at the wall plug
(Table III ), so INT8 is also the most efficient CPU precision on the
two nodes with energy measurements.

blocks.zh: III-C INT8 无 AVX2 支付; VNNI 添加更多

blocks.en:
The floor node, which has neither AVX2 nor VNNI, gains
1.45 × \times from INT8, more than the step node
(1.27 × \times ). This is consistent with a memory-bound

without wide integer instructions. Against the reference, the step node has
almost the same FP32 latency (33.80 vs
31.73 ms, the latter with a wider ± \pm 3.81 ms interval) and also carries AVX2, but its
INT8 latency is clearly higher (26.56 vs
20.75 ms). With the runtime and the IR held identical, the
additional INT8 acceleration on the reference points to VNNI rather than to AVX2.

blocks.en: III-D The Best Device Depends on the Hardware Class
blocks.zh: III-D 最佳设备取决于硬件类

blocks.en:
On the floor node the iGPU is far faster and more efficient than the CPU
(4.38 × \times faster and
5.46 × \times more efficient at the package at FP16; at the wall plug,
0.544 vs 3.014 J per inference), so the best
configuration there is the iGPU, at FP32 or FP16 alike. On the step node, whose CPU is much
stronger, the same iGPU barely helps
(1.04 × \times at FP32), and INT8 on the CPU
becomes the fastest configuration (26.56 ms). Its energy
matches FP16 on the iGPU at the package (0.859 vs

it shifts from the iGPU to the CPU as the CPU class improves
(Fig. 1 , Table III ).

blocks.en: III-E Implementation and Reproducibility
blocks.zh: 三-E 执行和可复制

blocks.en:
Two safeguards support reproducibility. First, every artifact along the chain
(checkpoint → \rightarrow ONNX → \rightarrow per-precision IR) is recorded in a
SHA-256 manifest, and a provenance gate re-checks this chain on disk before each
run, so every result traces back to the exact inputs that produced it. Second, the
integrated-GPU runtime is not assumed to work: we sweep OpenVINO and driver
combinations on the floor node and pin the first release (2024.6)
whose kernels the Gen9/11 iGPU can compile, as newer releases regressed a
normalization kernel to OpenCL 2.0 work-group functions that these devices
(driver 23.43.027642, OpenCL C 1.2) cannot build. A version-control
check confirms the pin does not bias the CPU numbers: FP32 and FP16 latency are
unchanged across releases (+1.0 % and
+0.1 %) while INT8 shifts by
+6.8 %. On the reference node the same check moves FP32, FP16 and INT8
by − - 5.1, − - 8.2 and
+12.2 %; all nodes are therefore measured on the
pinned release. IRs, calibration data and code are at the URL above.

blocks.en: IV Discussion and Conclusion
blocks.zh: 四. 讨论和结论

blocks.en:
Because INT8 does not cost
accuracy, precision can be chosen on cost alone, and the right choice depends on
the node. On a weak CPU without AVX2 the integrated GPU is the clear option, with
FP32 and FP16 equivalent there, whereas on a mainstream AVX2 CPU the integrated GPU adds
little and INT8 on the CPU is the fastest configuration and at least as
efficient as the integrated GPU. INT8 is faster on the CPU of every node, and on AVX2 CPUs
VNNI appears to add a further gain, so CPUs that expose it are the better choice
when INT8 is planned.

blocks.en:
We study a single ViT-S/16 encoder, so
the accuracy-neutral result and the magnitude of the speedups may differ for
other architectures or sizes. The reference node is a current laptop CPU,
included to place the edge nodes against present-day hardware rather than as an
edge target. As it is also the only node with VNNI, the VNNI observation rests on
two non-identical machines with a similar FP32 latency, not on a single
controlled variable. Device temperature was not recorded, so thermal
throttling cannot be ruled out directly, although the narrow confidence intervals
across repetitions on the edge nodes show no drift within a run. Extending this characterization to a set of
encoders, and to newer integrated GPUs and low-power CPUs that expose VNNI, is
left to future work.
